sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which fundamental Yoga practice involves the conscious regulation and control of breath to enhance vital energy?
questions.answer: B) Pranayama

questions.question_text: The primary objective of the 'Sports for All' framework is to:
options: A) Identify only elite athletes for international competitions
B) Provide equitable opportunities for physical activity to people of all ages and abilities
C) Commercialize local sporting events for profit
D) Focus solely on traditional indigenous sports
questions.answer: B) Provide equitable opportunities for physical activity to people of all ages and abilities

questions.question_text: In a standard game of Volleyball, what is the maximum number of contacts a team is allowed before the ball must be returned over the net?
questions.answer: B) Three

questions.question_text: State True or False: 'Surya Namaskar' (Sun Salutation) is a single, static posture rather than a dynamic sequence of asanas.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which concept refers to modifying sports rules, equipment, or environments so individuals with disabilities can safely and meaningfully participate?
questions.answer: B) Adaptive Physical Education

questions.question_text: In Basketball, how many points is a standard field goal worth if shot from inside the three-point arc?
questions.answer: B) Two points

questions.question_text: Which element of Ashtanga Yoga specifically deals with personal physical and mental observances, such as cleanliness and contentment?
questions.answer: A) Niyama

questions.question_text: State True or False: Implementing inclusive sports programs in schools primarily benefits only those students with disabilities.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a 'team sport' requiring complex tactical coordination among multiple players?
questions.answer: C) Football (Soccer)

questions.question_text: The regular practice of meditative Yoga (Dhyana) primarily contributes to personal excellence by improving:
options: C) Mental focus, emotional stability, and stress reduction
questions.answer: C) Mental focus, emotional stability, and stress reduction

questions.question_text: Define 'Inclusion' within the context of school physical education programs. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Inclusion is an educational approach ensuring all students, regardless of physical or cognitive abilities, learn and participate together in the same physical education environment using necessary adaptations.

questions.question_text: State the primary therapeutic benefit of practicing 'Shavasana' (Corpse Pose) at the end of a yoga session. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Shavasana deeply relaxes the central nervous system, lowers blood pressure, and allows the body to absorb the physical benefits of the preceding active asanas, promoting complete holistic recovery.

questions.question_text: List two essential safety equipment items required for a player participating in a Cricket match as a batsman. [10-20 words]
questions.answer: A batsman in cricket requires a protective helmet with a grill and padded leg guards (pads) to prevent severe injuries.

questions.question_text: Identify one major barrier to community sports participation for marginalized groups. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A major barrier is the lack of accessible infrastructure, meaning local facilities may not have ramps, adaptive equipment, or affordable programs designed for diverse economic and physical needs.

questions.question_text: What is the specific role of a 'Libero' in a Volleyball team? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Libero is a specialized defensive player restricted to the back row. They wear a contrasting jersey and excel at digging spikes and receiving serves to initiate team attacks.

questions.question_text: Explain how community engagement models in sports can successfully bridge social divides within a neighborhood. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Community sports models bring diverse demographic groups together for a shared goal. Through cooperative play, local tournaments, and volunteer coaching, participants build mutual trust, dismantle cultural prejudices, and foster strong, cohesive social networks within their neighborhoods.

questions.question_text: Describe the physiological and psychological benefits of practicing 'Tadasana' (Mountain Pose) for school-aged children. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Physiologically, Tadasana stretches the spine, corrects postural imbalances caused by heavy backpacks, and strengthens leg muscles. Psychologically, it enhances concentration, instills a sense of grounded stability, and improves overall bodily awareness during rapid developmental phases.

questions.question_text: Outline a basic offensive tactical layout (formation) utilized in Football (Soccer) and explain its primary goal. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The 4-3-3 formation features four defenders, three midfielders, and three forwards. Its primary offensive goal is to widen the play using wingers, overload the opponent's defense with rapid passing, and create numerous high-probability scoring opportunities inside the penalty area.

questions.question_text: Detail how an educator can modify a standard game of Basketball to make it fully inclusive for a student using a wheelchair. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: An educator can lower the height of the hoop, allow the student to hold the ball in their lap while pushing the chair (modifying the traveling rule), and create a safe spatial zone around the player to prevent aggressive contact.

questions.question_text: Analyze how the integration of the Eight Limbs of Yoga (Ashtanga) contributes directly to 'Personal Excellence' in a student's daily academic and personal life. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Ashtanga Yoga builds a holistic foundation for excellence. Yamas and Niyamas establish strong ethical discipline. Asanas ensure physical vitality, preventing illness. Pranayama and Pratyahara manage academic stress by controlling autonomic responses, while Dharana (concentration) directly improves focus during studies. Together, these limbs cultivate a balanced, resilient student capable of sustained high performance.

questions.question_text: A school wants to organize an inclusive community sports festival under the 'Sports for All' framework. Design a comprehensive plan detailing specific events, target demographics, and the necessary infrastructure adaptations required to ensure maximum participation. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The festival should target all age groups, including seniors and individuals with disabilities. Events include walking football, seated volleyball, and cooperative relay races. Infrastructure adaptations must include installing wheelchair ramps, providing auditory cues (beeping balls) for visually impaired participants, and ensuring all playing surfaces are smooth and hazard-free, guaranteeing equitable access for the entire community.
